subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should Telegram add an opt-in unauthorized-group-sender notice, and what default, cooldown, user-ID disclosure, and admin-contact contract should it use?
rationale: The request changes a security denial into visible group output and may disclose identifiers or amplify unauthorized traffic, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security policy.

options.title: Add an opt-in rate-limited notice
options.body: Keep the current silent default, add explicit configuration for the notice/template/admin contact, and throttle replies per chat/topic/sender before posting any user ID.

options.title: Fold into group admission design
options.body: Handle sender-facing instructions as part of the broader group-pairing and owner-notification contract tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/11489.

options.title: Keep silent denial
options.body: Reject visible group denial replies for now and document logs, /whoami, Bot API getUpdates, and existing allowlist setup as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Add an opt-in rate-limited notice
recommendation.body: Keep the current silent default, add explicit configuration for the notice/template/admin contact, and throttle replies per chat/topic/sender before posting any user ID.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing candidate for the Telegram authorization/security boundary from recent history and prior review context.
